## Summary

Modernizes and carries forward #913 on top of the current `os.Root` filesystem hardening.

- use native Git's filter-aware hashing when deciding whether committed files still have working-tree changes
- compare clean-filtered working-tree hashes directly with the processed commit's blob hashes, without refreshing the index
- batch candidate paths within conservative argv limits and retain successful hashes when another path fails
- retain the confined `worktreedir` / `osroot.ReadFileNoFollow` raw-hash fallback, including SHA-256 support
- modernize and expand the regression coverage

## Design

Native Git is the authority here because an `os.Root`-confined raw read cannot reproduce clean/smudge filter semantics. This does not remove the confinement boundary from Entire-owned filesystem access: Entire asks Git to hash repository-relative files and still uses the anchored raw read for any file Git cannot hash.

The Git operation lives in `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` and uses `git hash-object`, which applies path-specific clean filters without refreshing or rewriting the index. It scrubs hook-exported repository selectors that could override `-C`, splits large path sets across bounded commands, preserves successful results across partial failures, includes Git's stderr in diagnostics, and is bounded by `gitrepo.WorktreeContentHashBudget`.

The comparison uses the commit blob hashes already resolved by carry-forward detection. This remains correct if HEAD or the index moves after the processed commit. A design-pin test covers the case where both index and worktree have moved past that commit.

## Test evidence

The autocrlf regression test fails on unmodified main with:

```
Should be empty, but was [src/main.go]
autocrlf-only working tree differences should not be carried forward
```

After the fix:

- `mise run fmt` — pass
- `mise run lint` — pass
- `go build ./...` — pass
- `mise run test` — pass (10,994 tests, 8 skipped)

The standard macOS test invocation initially encountered four unrelated `/var` versus `/private/var` path-spelling assertions; the full suite passes with `TMPDIR` in its canonical `/private/var/...` spelling.

content.content:
3830520fe Authenticate the release-API lookup and stop the agent loop aborting

Two failures from the first real run of this workflow.

The Linux leg never got past install: install.sh resolves the nightly tag
through the GitHub releases API, and an unauthenticated call from a shared
runner IP is 403-ed by the 60/hour limit, which the script reports as
"check your internet connection". Both installers already honour
GITHUB_TOKEN; the workflow just never passed one.

The per-agent loop was written as `set -uo pipefail` on the assumption
that errexit was off, but GitHub invokes `shell: bash` as
`bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`. So the first failing agent
aborted the step before its result line was written and skipped every
agent after it — on Windows that silently cost the copilot-cli run. An
explicit `set +e` restores the intended behaviour: every agent runs, and
the Summarize step is what fails the job.

Also drops factoryai-droid from the Windows list for now. It fails there
and only there ("checkpoint state did not advance within 30s", twice
including the rerun) while passing on macOS, so it is a real finding
rather than a workflow bug and is tracked separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

f86b1a60c Give each agent its own step, timeout and key

The agents ran in one sequential loop inside a single step, bounded only
by the job's timeout-minutes. The mise task passes -timeout=30m and
--rerun-fails=1 runs it twice, so one hung agent could consume the whole
budget and every agent after it lost its verdict — and a job timeout also
skips Summarize and Upload despite if: always(), so the run would end
with no table and no artifacts.

One step per agent, each with timeout-minutes: 15, sized from run
34131195807 where the slowest pass was 2m40s. Steps carry
`!cancelled() && contains(env.AGENTS, ...)` so a killed step does not
skip the rest, and the job bound is now derived rather than guessed:
~3 min of setup plus six 15-minute steps plus summary and upload.
`timeout <N>m` was not an option — macOS runners have no timeout(1).

Summarize now iterates AGENTS rather than the result rows, because a step
killed by its own timeout writes no row and must show as a failure rather
than vanish from the table.

Each step carries only the key its agent needs, which retires the
codex_model shell hack. That is defence in depth rather than isolation:
bootstrap persists credentials to a shared HOME (~/.claude/.claude.json
and ~/.factory/settings.json, both 0644, same uid), so a later agent can
still read them off disk. Closing that needs a HOME per agent or a job
per agent; the findings asking for it stay open deliberately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

# Nightly Install Smoke run 34583415795: two defects, two PRs

## Context

Run https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34583415795 (schedule, 2026-09-11) failed on
`smoke (windows-latest)`. Two independent problems:

1. **Workflow reporting.** Every "Smoke test <agent>" step is green even when its agent failed;
   only "Summarize" turns red. Reader has to open the step summary to learn *which* agent failed.
2. **Real CLI regression on Windows for Copilot CLI.** `TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli`
   fails (both attempts) with `shadow branches should be cleaned up within 10s after commit,
   found: [entire/6503d24-e3b0c4]`. Linux and macOS pass; the previous nightly
   (`v0.10.7-nightly.202609100626.0138471ae`, run 34459813849) passed on Windows.

### 1. Why the agent step is green and Summarize is red

`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`, steps "Smoke test …" (lines 208–317). Each body is:

```bash
set +e
…
mise run test:e2e --agent "$AGENT" "$TEST_FILTER"
rc=$?
grep -q '^Total: 0 ' … && rc=1
echo "$AGENT $rc" >> e2e/artifacts/results.txt     # last command → step exit 0
```

`set +e` was added in 3830520fe when all agents ran in ONE loop step, so one failure would not
abort the loop ("the Summarize step is what fails the job"). f86b1a60c then split the loop into
one step per agent gated on `!cancelled()`, but kept the body verbatim. Nothing ever propagates
`rc`, so the step's exit status is that of the trailing `echo`. The per-step gating already
makes propagating it safe: `!cancelled()` runs later agent steps after a failed one, and
Summarize/Upload are `always()`. Only the *display* is wrong; the job verdict and Slack notify
are unchanged.

### 2. Why Copilot on Windows leaves a shadow branch

Evidence from the artifacts (`nightly-smoke-windows-latest` for both runs, `entire.log`):

| | passing nightly 0138471ae | failing nightly 5f09e04de |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post-commit → `session condensed`, `shadow branch deleted` | yes | yes |
| post-commit `files_touched_before` (copilot) | 0 | **1** |
| agent-stop, 2s after the commit | `no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint` | `files changed during session modified=1` → `created shadow branch … entire/6503d24-e3b0c4` |

Same on Linux in the failing run: "no files modified". Same Copilot version both nights
(`npm view @github/copilot dist-tags` → latest 1.0.83 since 2026-09-04). Codex on Windows already
had `files_touched_before=1` on the passing night, so the 0→1 flip is Copilot-specific.

Chain:

- **Trigger — PR #2341 (`feat(copilot-cli): track subagent tasks`, merge 5f09e04de, the exact
  commit the failing nightly was cut from).** `copilotcli/transcript.go`
  `extractModifiedFilesMatching` now falls back to `toolTelemetry.restrictedProperties.filePaths`
  when `properties.filePaths` is empty. Copilot 1.0.83 puts the paths there, so Entire's Copilot
  transcript analyzer went from returning nothing to returning `docs/blue.md`. This is a correct
  improvement; it exposed a latent bug.
- **Bug — `filterToUncommittedFiles` (`cmd/entire/cli/state.go:332`)** is the turn-end guard
  that drops transcript-reported files already committed mid-turn. It compares
  `readWorktreeFileSafely` raw bytes with `headFile.Contents()` (`string(working) != head`,
  line 388). The e2e repo sets `core.autocrlf=true` (`e2e/testutil/repo.go:88`, and it is the
  Git-for-Windows default). Copilot's Create tool writes CRLF on Windows; `git add` stores LF.
  Raw bytes ≠ blob → file "still uncommitted" → `SaveStep` mints `entire/<newHEAD>-e3b0c4` after
  condensation already ran. Nothing condenses it again (the turn is over), so it outlives the
  session. On Linux Copilot writes LF, so the comparison happens to match.
- **Precedent — PR #2336 (`Handle autocrlf in carry-forward detection`, #913)** fixed the same
  class of bug on the post-commit path: `strategy/content_overlap.go:513-547` hashes worktree
  candidates through `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` (`git hash-object`, filter-aware) and falls back
  to the confined raw hash `workingTreeMatchesBlob` only when git cannot hash the path. The
  turn-end filter was never converted. The second caller of the filter (subagent capture,
  `lifecycle.go:1897`) has the same exposure.

## Plan

Two isolated PRs (one objective each).

### PR A — workflow: put the verdict on the agent's own step (this branch, `fix-nightly-smoke-test`)

File: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`.

1. Append `exit "$rc"` as the last line of each of the six "Smoke test …" bodies (they must stay
   byte-identical apart from `AGENT`/key, as the header comment promises).
2. Update the header comment (lines 197–198): `set +e` still exists so the result row is written
   before the step reports; the trailing `exit "$rc"` makes the agent's own step carry its
   verdict; later steps run anyway because they are gated on `!cancelled()`, and Summarize stays
   the aggregate table. Drop nothing else; Summarize logic is unchanged (it still covers the
   timed-out-no-row case).

### PR B — CLI: make the turn-end committed-file filter clean-filter aware (separate branch off main)

TDD order.

1. **Failing test first** — `cmd/entire/cli/state_test.go`, next to
   `TestFilterToUncommittedFiles_ReallyModified` (same shape: `t.Chdir(tmpDir)`, no
   `t.Parallel()` because `openRepository` resolves from cwd; `testutil.InitRepo`). Mirror
   `TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges_AutocrlfNormalizedWorkingTree`
   (`strategy/content_overlap_test.go:424-466`): `testutil.RunGit config core.autocrlf true`,
   write a CRLF file, `RunGit add` + `RunGit commit` (native git, so the clean filter applies),
   assert `RunGit diff --exit-code` is clean, then
   `filterToUncommittedFiles(ctx, []string{"file.txt"}, tmpDir)` must be empty. Fails on main
   with `[file.txt]`.
2. **Extract the shared comparison** from `strategy/content_overlap.go` lines 513–547 into one
   exported helper in the same file, e.g.

   ```go
   type CommittedBlob struct { Hash plumbing.Hash; Mode filemode.FileMode }
   // WorktreeMatchesCommitted reports per path whether the clean-filtered working-tree
   // content hashes to the committed blob (native git hash-object; confined raw-hash
   // fallback for paths git cannot hash and for symlink blobs).
   func WorktreeMatchesCommitted(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string, files map[string]CommittedBlob) map[string]bool
   ```

   It owns the `requiresConfinedWorktreeHash` split, the `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` batch, the
   existing warning on partial hash failure, and the `workingTreeMatchesBlob` fallback.
   `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges` calls it for its `candidates` (behaviour unchanged; existing
   `TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges_*` tests pin it).
3. **Use it in `filterToUncommittedFiles`** (`cli` already imports `strategy`): build
   `map[path]CommittedBlob` from `headTree.File(relPath)` (`.Hash`, `.Mode`); keep files absent
   from HEAD (unchanged, fail-open); keep files the helper reports as not matching; drop the
   `readWorktreeFileSafely` + string comparison. Keep every fail-open branch. Both callers
   (`lifecycle.go:965`, `lifecycle.go:1897`) are fixed by this one change.
4. **Docs** — `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md` "Content-Aware Carry-Forward"
   (line ~222): one sentence that the turn-end committed-file filter uses the same native-git
   comparison, so autocrlf cannot resurrect a shadow branch after a mid-turn commit.

## Verification

PR A:
- `gh workflow run nightly-e2e.yml --ref fix-nightly-smoke-test` (user-triggered: real agent
  calls, costs tokens). Expected: on Windows the red X lands on "Smoke test copilot-cli" while
  the following steps and Summarize still run and the table is unchanged. Until PR B ships in a
  nightly, the run keeps failing for the right reason on the right step.

PR B:
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ -run 'TestFilterToUncommittedFiles' -count=1` — new autocrlf test
  fails before step 2/3, passes after; `_ReallyModified` still passes.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/ -run 'TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges' -count=1` —
  unchanged after the extraction.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`, then `mise run test`.
- Real-world confirmation is the next scheduled nightly after the fix is in a nightly tag
  (Windows copilot-cli row goes green), or a user-run
  `mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli TestMultiSessionSequential` on a Windows machine.

`smoke (windows-latest)`. Two independent problems:

1. **Workflow reporting.** Every "Smoke test <agent>" step is green even when its agent failed;
   only "Summarize" turns red. Reader has to open the step summary to learn *which* agent failed.
2. **Real CLI regression on Windows for Copilot CLI.** `TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli`
   fails (both attempts) with `shadow branches should be cleaned up within 10s after commit,
   found: [entire/6503d24-e3b0c4]`. Linux and macOS pass; the previous nightly
   (`v0.10.7-nightly.202609100626.0138471ae`, run 34459813849) passed on Windows.

### 1. Why the agent step is green and Summarize is red

`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`, steps "Smoke test …" (lines 208–317). Each body is:

```bash
set +e
…
mise run test:e2e --agent "$AGENT" "$TEST_FILTER"
rc=$?
grep -q '^Total: 0 ' … && rc=1
echo "$AGENT $rc" >> e2e/artifacts/results.txt     # last command → step exit 0
```

`set +e` was added in 3830520fe when all agents ran in ONE loop step, so one failure would not
abort the loop ("the Summarize step is what fails the job"). f86b1a60c then split the loop into
one step per agent gated on `!cancelled()`, but kept the body verbatim. Nothing ever propagates
`rc`, so the step's exit status is that of the trailing `echo`. The per-step gating already
makes propagating it safe: `!cancelled()` runs later agent steps after a failed one, and
Summarize/Upload are `always()`. Only the *display* is wrong; the job verdict and Slack notify
are unchanged.

### 2. Why Copilot on Windows leaves a shadow branch

Evidence from the artifacts (`nightly-smoke-windows-latest` for both runs, `entire.log`):

| | passing nightly 0138471ae | failing nightly 5f09e04de |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post-commit → `session condensed`, `shadow branch deleted` | yes | yes |
| post-commit `files_touched_before` (copilot) | 0 | **1** |
| agent-stop, 2s after the commit | `no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint` | `files changed during session modified=1` → `created shadow branch … entire/6503d24-e3b0c4` |

Same on Linux in the failing run: "no files modified". Same Copilot version both nights
(`npm view @github/copilot dist-tags` → latest 1.0.83 since 2026-09-04). Codex on Windows already
had `files_touched_before=1` on the passing night, so the 0→1 flip is Copilot-specific.

Chain:

- **Trigger — PR #2341 (`feat(copilot-cli): track subagent tasks`, merge 5f09e04de, the exact
  commit the failing nightly was cut from).** `copilotcli/transcript.go`
  `extractModifiedFilesMatching` now falls back to `toolTelemetry.restrictedProperties.filePaths`
  when `properties.filePaths` is empty. Copilot 1.0.83 puts the paths there, so Entire's Copilot
  transcript analyzer went from returning nothing to returning `docs/blue.md`. This is a correct
  improvement; it exposed a latent bug.
- **Bug — `filterToUncommittedFiles` (`cmd/entire/cli/state.go:332`)** is the turn-end guard
  that drops transcript-reported files already committed mid-turn. It compares
  `readWorktreeFileSafely` raw bytes with `headFile.Contents()` (`string(working) != head`,
  line 388). The e2e repo sets `core.autocrlf=true` (`e2e/testutil/repo.go:88`, and it is the
  Git-for-Windows default). Copilot's Create tool writes CRLF on Windows; `git add` stores LF.
  Raw bytes ≠ blob → file "still uncommitted" → `SaveStep` mints `entire/<newHEAD>-e3b0c4` after
  condensation already ran. Nothing condenses it again (the turn is over), so it outlives the
  session. On Linux Copilot writes LF, so the comparison happens to match.
- **Precedent — PR #2336 (`Handle autocrlf in carry-forward detection`, #913)** fixed the same
  class of bug on the post-commit path: `strategy/content_overlap.go:513-547` hashes worktree
  candidates through `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` (`git hash-object`, filter-aware) and falls back
  to the confined raw hash `workingTreeMatchesBlob` only when git cannot hash the path. The
  turn-end filter was never converted. The second caller of the filter (subagent capture,
  `lifecycle.go:1897`) has the same exposure.

## Plan

Two isolated PRs (one objective each).

### PR A — workflow: put the verdict on the agent's own step (this branch, `fix-nightly-smoke-test`)

File: `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml`.

1. Append `exit "$rc"` as the last line of each of the six "Smoke test …" bodies (they must stay
   byte-identical apart from `AGENT`/key, as the header comment promises).
2. Update the header comment (lines 197–198): `set +e` still exists so the result row is written
   before the step reports; the trailing `exit "$rc"` makes the agent's own step carry its
   verdict; later steps run anyway because they are gated on `!cancelled()`, and Summarize stays
   the aggregate table. Drop nothing else; Summarize logic is unchanged (it still covers the
   timed-out-no-row case).

### PR B — CLI: make the turn-end committed-file filter clean-filter aware (separate branch off main)

TDD order.

1. **Failing test first** — `cmd/entire/cli/state_test.go`, next to
   `TestFilterToUncommittedFiles_ReallyModified` (same shape: `t.Chdir(tmpDir)`, no
   `t.Parallel()` because `openRepository` resolves from cwd; `testutil.InitRepo`). Mirror
   `TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges_AutocrlfNormalizedWorkingTree`
   (`strategy/content_overlap_test.go:424-466`): `testutil.RunGit config core.autocrlf true`,
   write a CRLF file, `RunGit add` + `RunGit commit` (native git, so the clean filter applies),
   assert `RunGit diff --exit-code` is clean, then
   `filterToUncommittedFiles(ctx, []string{"file.txt"}, tmpDir)` must be empty. Fails on main
   with `[file.txt]`.
2. **Extract the shared comparison** from `strategy/content_overlap.go` lines 513–547 into one
   exported helper in the same file, e.g.

   ```go
   type CommittedBlob struct { Hash plumbing.Hash; Mode filemode.FileMode }
   // WorktreeMatchesCommitted reports per path whether the clean-filtered working-tree
   // content hashes to the committed blob (native git hash-object; confined raw-hash
   // fallback for paths git cannot hash and for symlink blobs).
   func WorktreeMatchesCommitted(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string, files map[string]CommittedBlob) map[string]bool
   ```

   It owns the `requiresConfinedWorktreeHash` split, the `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` batch, the
   existing warning on partial hash failure, and the `workingTreeMatchesBlob` fallback.
   `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges` calls it for its `candidates` (behaviour unchanged; existing
   `TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges_*` tests pin it).
3. **Use it in `filterToUncommittedFiles`** (`cli` already imports `strategy`): build
   `map[path]CommittedBlob` from `headTree.File(relPath)` (`.Hash`, `.Mode`); keep files absent
   from HEAD (unchanged, fail-open); keep files the helper reports as not matching; drop the
   `readWorktreeFileSafely` + string comparison. Keep every fail-open branch. Both callers
   (`lifecycle.go:965`, `lifecycle.go:1897`) are fixed by this one change.
4. **Docs** — `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md` "Content-Aware Carry-Forward"
   (line ~222): one sentence that the turn-end committed-file filter uses the same native-git
   comparison, so autocrlf cannot resurrect a shadow branch after a mid-turn commit.

## Verification

PR A:
- `gh workflow run nightly-e2e.yml --ref fix-nightly-smoke-test` (user-triggered: real agent
  calls, costs tokens). Expected: on Windows the red X lands on "Smoke test copilot-cli" while
  the following steps and Summarize still run and the table is unchanged. Until PR B ships in a
  nightly, the run keeps failing for the right reason on the right step.

PR B:
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ -run 'TestFilterToUncommittedFiles' -count=1` — new autocrlf test
  fails before step 2/3, passes after; `_ReallyModified` still passes.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/ -run 'TestFilesWithRemainingAgentChanges' -count=1` —
  unchanged after the extraction.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`, then `mise run test`.
- Real-world confirmation is the next scheduled nightly after the fix is in a nightly tag
  (Windows copilot-cli row goes green), or a user-run
  `mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli TestMultiSessionSequential` on a Windows machine.

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

input.command:
f=.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml && grep -c '^          echo "\$AGENT \$rc" >> e2e/artifacts/results.txt$' "$f" && sed -i '' 's|^          echo "\$AGENT \$rc" >> e2e/artifacts/results.txt$|&\n          exit "$rc"|' "$f" && python3 - "$f" <<'EOF'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p).read()
old = """      # In each body: `set +e` because GitHub already runs `shell: bash` with
      # -e, which would end the step before its result row is written. The
      # `Total: 0` check because a filter matching no test exits 0 with "[no
      # tests to run]", which would report every agent as passing. Per-agent
      # E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR because the mise task otherwise derives one shared dir
      # and later agents overwrite earlier reports.
"""
new = """      # In each body: `set +e` because GitHub already runs `shell: bash` with
      # -e, which would end the step before its result row is written; the
      # closing `exit "$rc"` then reports the agent's own verdict on its own
      # step, and the `!cancelled()` gates above are what keep the later agents
      # running after it fails. The `Total: 0` check because a filter matching
      # no test exits 0 with "[no tests to run]", which would report every
      # agent as passing. Per-agent E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR because the mise task
      # otherwise derives one shared dir and later agents overwrite earlier
      # reports.
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1, s.count(old)
open(p, "w").write(s.replace(old, new))
EOF
git diff --stat && git diff | head -80

// TestFilterToUncommittedFiles_AutocrlfNormalizedWorkingTree pins that the
// filter agrees with git about what is committed: under core.autocrlf=true the
// committed blob is LF-normalized while the working tree keeps CRLF, and git
// reports the file clean.
func TestFilterToUncommittedFiles_AutocrlfNormalizedWorkingTree(t *testing.T) {
	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
	t.Chdir(tmpDir)

	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)
	testutil.RunGit(t, tmpDir, "config", "core.autocrlf", "true")

	const content = "# Blue\r\n\r\nBlue is a colour.\r\n"
	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "blue.md", content)
	testutil.RunGit(t, tmpDir, "add", "--", "blue.md")
	testutil.RunGit(t, tmpDir, "commit", "-m", "Add blue")

	testutil.RunGit(t, tmpDir, "diff", "--exit-code", "--", "blue.md")
	disk, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(tmpDir, "blue.md"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, content, string(disk), "the working tree must retain CRLF bytes")

	result := filterToUncommittedFiles(context.Background(), []string{"blue.md"}, tmpDir)
	require.Empty(t, result, "autocrlf-only working tree differences are not uncommitted changes")
}
EOF

Report each agent's smoke verdict on its own step

`!cancelled()`, which already keeps the later agents running after a failed
one, so ending each body with `exit "$rc"` puts the verdict where the reader
looks while Summarize keeps the aggregate table.

description: "Orphan mise shims (entire-agent-devin, entire-agent-kilo) in ~/.local/share/mise/shims make the nine TestRunUninstall_* tests fail under a full cmd/entire/cli package run on this Mac; pass in isolation"

Sept 2026: `mise run test:ci` failed only in `cmd/entire/cli`, nine `TestRunUninstall_*`
tests with "uninstall did not complete", also on a clean origin/main worktree. Cause (captured
stderr): `could not check whether Devin hooks are installed: mise ERROR No version is set for
shim: entire-agent-devin`. Two mise shim files had no installed tool behind them, so the
external-agent probe failed, the agent became "unchecked", and runUninstall refused to claim
completion. `mise reshim` does not remove orphans; deleting the two files fixed it and
`~/go/bin` / `~/wks/external-agents/bin` binaries took over.

**Why:** Looks like a code regression but is machine state; the tests pass in isolation, so
`-run` narrows it away and hides the cause.

**How to apply:** If `TestRunUninstall_*` fail only in the full package run, check
`ls ~/.local/share/mise/shims | grep entire-agent` against `mise ls -i` before suspecting the
branch. Related: [[lint-binary-shadow]] (same class: stale binaries ahead of mise's on PATH).

Both fixes are committed, one per branch, and nothing has been pushed.

**Why the agent step was green and Summarize red.** Each "Smoke test" body runs under `set +e`, stores the test's exit code in a variable, appends a result row, and ends. The trailing `echo` is the last command, so the step always exits 0. That `set +e` dates from when all agents ran in one loop step. The later split into per-agent steps gated on `!cancelled()` kept the body verbatim, so nothing ever propagated the code. The fix appends `exit "$rc"` to all six bodies and updates the header comment. Later agent steps still run after a failure because of `!cancelled()`, and Summarize keeps the aggregate table. Committed as f15fe6926 on `fix-nightly-smoke-test`. actionlint reports only the pre-existing `copilot-requests` permission scope it does not know yet.

**Why Copilot on Windows leaves a shadow branch.** The failing nightly tag was cut at the merge of PR #2341. Comparing both nights' Windows logs, everything matches until the agent-stop hook two seconds after Copilot's own commit:

- Passing night: "no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint".
- Failing night: one modified file, then a new shadow branch on the new HEAD that nothing condenses again.

PR #2341 made Copilot's transcript parser read `restrictedProperties.filePaths`, so Entire now learns which file Copilot wrote. The turn-end guard `filterToUncommittedFiles` in `cmd/entire/cli/state.go` then compared raw worktree bytes with the HEAD blob. The e2e repo sets `core.autocrlf=true`, Copilot writes CRLF on Windows, git stores LF, so the committed file looked uncommitted. Linux passes only because Copilot writes LF there. Copilot's npm version was identical on both nights. PR #2336 had already fixed this class of bug on the post-commit path with filter-aware `git hash-object` hashing.

The fix extracts that comparison into `strategy.WorktreeMatchesCommitted`, uses it from both the carry-forward path and the turn-end filter, adds a failing-first autocrlf regression test, and documents it in checkpoint-scenarios.md. Committed as 857c5519e on `fix/turn-end-committed-filter-autocrlf` in the new worktree at `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/fix-turn-end-autocrlf`.

**Verification.** The new test fails on main with `[blue.md]` and passes with the fix. `mise run check` ran on the CLI branch: lint reports 0 issues and every package passes except nine `TestRunUninstall_*` tests in `cmd/entire/cli`. Those fail because stale `entire-agent-devin` and `entire-agent-kilo` mise shims reappeared on this Mac today; the same package passes in full with the shims hidden from PATH and the tests pass in isolation. Deleting the two shim files is the known remedy.

**What remains.** The nightly keeps failing on Windows until the CLI fix reaches a nightly tag; after PR A merges, the red mark will at least land on the copilot-cli step. Say the word and I will push both branches and open the two PRs.

Justification:
1. `requiresConfinedWorktreeHash` returns true for `filemode.Symlink` before any `Lstat` (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/content_overlap.go:597-599`), so the path is never handed to `HashWorktreeFiles` and always lands in the fallback.
2. `workingTreeMatchesBlob` branches on `commitMode == filemode.Symlink` alone and calls `root.Readlink(name)`, returning false on error (`content_overlap.go:631-636`); it never consults the on-disk type. `os.Root.Readlink` on a regular file errors on every platform (Windows: not a reparse point), so `matches[path] = false`.
3. Git docs for `core.symlinks` (default false on Git for Windows): "symbolic links are checked out as small plain files that contain the link text. git-update-index and git-add will not change the recorded type to regular file" — implemented by `ce_mode_from_stat` preserving `S_IFLNK` from the existing index entry. `git status` then hashes the plain file's bytes against the symlink blob and reports it clean. Confidence: high.
4. Old code (`state.go` deleted hunk) used `readWorktreeFileSafely` → `osroot.ReadFileNoFollow` (`trail_review_cmd.go:1018-1034`), which on Windows reads the plain file's bytes `CLAUDE.md` and compares them to `headFile.Contents()` = `CLAUDE.md` → equal → dropped. So the Windows behaviour flips from "committed" to "uncommitted". Note the inverse: on Unix the old `ReadFileNoFollow` failed on a real symlink and kept the path, and the new `Readlink` path now drops it correctly — this PR fixes Unix while breaking Windows/`core.symlinks=false`.
5. Trigger: `relModifiedFiles` is transcript-extracted `modifiedFiles` merged with `git status` Modified (`lifecycle.go:952-965`). Judge "already committed" at turn end the way git does

filterToUncommittedFiles is the turn-end guard that drops transcript-reported
files an agent committed mid-turn, so SaveStep does not mint a shadow branch
after post-commit has already condensed the session and deleted the old one.
It compared raw working-tree bytes with the HEAD blob, so under
core.autocrlf=true a CRLF working copy of the LF-normalized blob counted as
uncommitted. Copilot CLI writes CRLF on Windows, and PR #2341 made its
transcript analyzer report the files it writes, which turned the latent
mismatch into a shadow branch that nothing condenses (nightly run
34583415795, TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli on windows-latest;
Linux passes only because Copilot writes LF there).

The post-commit carry-forward path already answers the same question with
native git hash-object (#2336). Extract that comparison into
strategy.WorktreeMatchesCommitted and use it from both call sites; the
subagent capture path shares the guard and is fixed by the same change.

Two cases hash-object alone gets wrong keep the raw-bytes comparison as a
second acceptance path rather than a fallback: a blob that already carries
CRLF, which git status exempts from autocrlf conversion while hash-object
converts unconditionally, and a symlink blob checked out as a regular file
under core.symlinks=false, where Readlink has nothing to read. Both are
pinned by tests alongside the turn-end autocrlf case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
